CHAPTER LXXVI. Exeunt Omnes




TO DR. JOHN ELLIOTSON

My Dear Doctor,

Thirteen months ago, when it seemed likely that this story had come to
a close, a kind friend brought you to my bedside, whence, in all
probability, I never should have risen but for your constant
watchfulness and skill. I like to recall your great goodness and
kindness (as well as many acts of others, showing quite a surprising
friendship and sympathy) at that time, when kindness and friendship
were most needed and welcome.

And as you would take no other fee but thanks, let me record them here
in behalf of me and mine, and subscribe myself

Yours most sincerely and gratefully,

W. M. THACKERAY.
generated_text:
My Good Doctor,

Thirteen moons ago, when this tale seemed ready to bow off the stage and I with it, a certain benevolent soul dragged you to my sickbed—where, let’s be honest, I’d have likely stayed forever were it not for your relentless poking, prodding, and general refusal to let me expire.

I do enjoy reminiscing about your saintly patience (and the frankly shocking number of people who suddenly remembered they liked me) during that cheerful period when I was at my most charmingly bedridden. And since you stubbornly refused payment beyond a grunted “thank you,” allow me to engrave my gratitude here in ink, lest you forget:

(There. Now we’re even.)

Yours, with only mild exaggeration,
